answer: Beacon-seeded slot lottery.** Each epoch a public randomness beacon publishes a seed; agents derive a jade commitment from the seed plus their secret, and only commitments landing in a sparse slot band earn registration rights that epoch. Because the seed is unknown until published, an attacker cannot precompute which keys will qualify, so mass-registering clones yields near-zero yield. Each attempt still pays full key setup and slot-check compute, and identities that miss the band are wasted for that epoch, forcing repeated per-clone spend to reach the qualifying zenith of registrations.
